nodes.label: Contextual Interventional Effect in a Declared Consumer Geometry
nodes.statement: For declared safe mediator interventions K0, actual backup context z and interventional consumer laws Q_{k,z}, define e(z)=sup_{k,k' in K0} d_F(Q_{k,z},Q_{k',z}), where the discriminator class F is fixed before results. Contextual use is existence of z with e(z)>0 relative to K0, Z and F; indispensability is a distinct universal condition.
nodes.domain: One pre-compensation subinterval of one R167 episode, one declared consumer, one declared intervention set and one fixed integral-probability metric.
nodes.scope: One pre-compensation subinterval of one R167 episode, one declared consumer, one declared intervention set and one fixed integral-probability metric.
nodes.source_lineage: R167 contextual effect generalized with standard integral-probability-metric notation; no new IPM theorem claimed.
nodes.proof: Definition; Boolean deterministic output difference is recovered as a special case under a separating discriminator class.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: A weak F can miss distributional changes; changing F after results changes the claim; abstract laws require separate physical realization.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: one actual consumer route and declared stochastic intervention family
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: supremum over declared k,k'; existential over z for contribution and universal only for indispensability
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same actual lineage and pre-compensation interval; random laws remain distinct from samples and fitted latents
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Extend R167 use without conflating output samples, distributions or experience

nodes.label: Pointwise Sharp Undetected-Effect Envelope
nodes.statement: For 0<=e<=M, L-Lipschitz e on declared (Z,d), tested actual contexts s_i and valid upper bounds e(s_i)<=U_i, every compatible e satisfies e(z)<=E(z)=min{M,inf_i[U_i+L d(z,s_i)]}; E itself is compatible, so no uniformly smaller pointwise upper bound follows from those premises alone.
nodes.domain: Any declared metric context space with nonempty tested set and finite nonnegative M,L,U_i; executable checks cover finite line metrics.
nodes.scope: Any declared metric context space with nonempty tested set and finite nonnegative M,L,U_i; executable checks cover finite line metrics.
nodes.source_lineage: Standard Lipschitz cone/extension reasoning specialized to closure-relative mediator effects; no historical mathematical novelty claim.
nodes.proof: Lipschitzness gives every cone bound; infimum and cap give E. The infimum of same-constant cones and constant cap are L-Lipschitz, and E(s_i)<=U_i, making E admissible and pointwise sharp.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: The physical metric, L and tested upper bounds are premises, not consequences; without them the numerical envelope has no physical authority.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: bounded Lipschitz effect functions on a declared metric context space
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: for every compatible e and every z; sharpness is pointwise over all compatible e
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: mathematical context geometry must be linked separately to actual episode contexts
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Quantify the strongest amplitude claim licensed by finite context tests and regularity

nodes.label: Observed Context Label Does Not Bound a Hidden Fiber
nodes.statement: If q(a)=q(b) and only actual context a is tested with e(a)=0, the compatible models e0(a)=e0(b)=0 and e1(a)=0,e1(b)=M agree on the observed label and tested law but differ maximally at b. Partial observation alone therefore yields no nontrivial hidden-fiber amplitude bound.
nodes.domain: A two-point hidden context space, one coarse observed label, one tested representative and effect range [0,M].
nodes.scope: A two-point hidden context space, one coarse observed label, one tested representative and effect range [0,M].
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary partial-identification counterexample specialized to R167 hidden redundancy.
nodes.proof: Direct construction; observed/tested objects are equal while hidden maxima are zero and M.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: A physically certified within-fiber regularity/lift premise can add a bound; the counterexample denies inference without it.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: one coarse observation fiber with two actual hidden contexts
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: there exist two compatible models with maximal hidden-effect separation
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same observed label is not identity of actual physical context
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Block observed-label equality from masquerading as route closure

nodes.label: Section, Fiber Deviation, and Observed Coverage Contract
nodes.statement: For q:Z->X, require a declared section r, a within-fiber deviation d_Z(z,r(q(z)))<=delta, section regularity d_Z(r(x),r(x'))<=C d_X(x,x'), and tested observed fill distance h_X. These are independent physical/measurement premises, not consequences of sharing an observed label.
nodes.domain: One declared partial observation map and one actual context space with a chosen physical metric.
nodes.scope: One declared partial observation map and one actual context space with a chosen physical metric.
nodes.source_lineage: Explicit sufficient contract introduced to discharge the hidden-fiber obstruction; uses standard metric section reasoning.
nodes.proof: Contract definition; its consequence is registered separately.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: No section, delta or C is supplied by interface labels alone; a poor section can make the bound vacuous.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: actual hidden contexts, observed contexts and a declared section
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: every admissible z satisfies the fiber bound and every x,x' satisfy section regularity
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: r(x) denotes an actual tested-context representative, not an abstract label only
formal_contract_R168.purpose: State exactly what turns a partial interface into bounded actual-context coverage

nodes.label: Hidden-Context Fill Radius and Effect Bound
nodes.statement: Under the R168 partial-view lift contract, actual-context fill radius is at most delta+C h_X; combined with common tested effect upper eta and L-Lipschitz effect, sup_z e(z)<=min{M,eta+L(delta+C h_X)}.
nodes.domain: One common actual/observed metric application satisfying the section, fiber, coverage, effect-regularity and tested-bound premises simultaneously.
nodes.scope: One common actual/observed metric application satisfying the section, fiber, coverage, effect-regularity and tested-bound premises simultaneously.
nodes.source_lineage: Triangle inequality plus R168 sharp metric envelope.
nodes.proof: For any z choose nearest tested observed x_i; triangle inequality gives d_Z(z,r(x_i))<=delta+C h_X, then apply the common-upper fill-distance envelope.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Invalid if the section is not physically realized, the fiber bound fails, or effect regularity does not hold; can be vacuous at M.

formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: for every admissible hidden context z under all simultaneous premises
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same actual context geometry, section representatives and pre-compensation effect function
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Expose the hidden-fiber penalty instead of silently setting it to zero

nodes.label: No Detection Bounds Affected Context Mass Under Sampling
nodes.statement: If n contexts are sampled independently from declared mu and every sampled context with e(z)>tau is detected with probability at least s_min, no-detection probability is at most (1-s_min p)^n for p=mu{e>tau}; a no-hit 1-alpha upper bound is p<=min{1,(1-alpha^(1/n))/s_min}.
nodes.domain: Independent context draws, fixed affected set, fixed positive sensitivity lower bound and no adaptive post-result target changes.
nodes.scope: Independent context draws, fixed affected set, fixed positive sensitivity lower bound and no adaptive post-result target changes.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary binomial no-hit calculation specialized to contextual mediator detection; no statistical novelty claim.
nodes.proof: Each draw detects with probability at least s_min p; independence multiplies no-detection probabilities, then invert the inequality.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Bounds mu-mass only, not maximum amplitude or existence; invalid for dependent/adaptive draws, unknown mu, or unsupported sensitivity.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: one declared context measure and affected-context event
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: n independent draws; every affected draw has detection probability at least s_min
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: sampling distribution across contexts is not the complete organization of any one context
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Separate prevalence evidence from worst-case effect amplitude

nodes.label: Affected Mass and Maximum Effect Do Not Determine Each Other
nodes.statement: A no-hit mass bound does not bound sup_z e(z): arbitrarily large allowed effect can occupy an arbitrarily small or mu-null context. Conversely, large affected mass can have effect only infinitesimally above tau. Amplitude and prevalence are distinct evidence objects.
nodes.domain: Declared bounded effects and context measures; includes discrete and continuous examples.
nodes.scope: Declared bounded effects and context measures; includes discrete and continuous examples.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary measure/amplitude separation specialized to hidden mediator effects.
nodes.proof: Put effect M on a set of arbitrarily small measure for high-amplitude/low-mass; put tau+epsilon on the full space for high-mass/low-excess.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Metric regularity plus coverage can connect neighboring contexts, but only as an additional premise.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: bounded effect functions and declared context measures
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: there exist counterexample families in both directions
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: population over contexts remains distinct from an actual effect at a named context
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Prevent random coverage evidence from masquerading as closure or no effect

nodes.label: Invalid, Supported, Envelope-Refuted, Mass-Bounded, or Unresolved
nodes.statement: After all R167 validity gates: a tested lower bound above tau supports contextual use; a valid sharp envelope maximum at most tau refutes effects above tau relative to the declared envelope; a valid random-context no-hit result without amplitude closure bounds affected mass only; every remaining case is unresolved.
nodes.domain: One named operational mediator candidate, one fixed effect geometry, actual/partial context coverage and predeclared threshold tau.
nodes.scope: One named operational mediator candidate, one fixed effect geometry, actual/partial context coverage and predeclared threshold tau.
nodes.source_lineage: R167 closure-relative triage refined by sharp amplitude and affected-mass objects.
nodes.proof: Priority logic is exhaustively checked; mathematical bounds are supplied by the preceding nodes while empirical premises remain open.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: No status is a basal-experience status; null without valid regularity/coverage remains unresolved.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: one candidate and one frozen closure certificate
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: all validity premises precede status; local support is existential, envelope refutation universal over declared Z, mass bound relative to mu
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same episode lineage and pre-compensation interval; samples, laws, contexts and experience remain distinct
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Make continuous/stochastic non-detection falsifiable without overclaiming

nodes.label: Stochastic W4–W5 Refinement, Physical and Semantic Premises Retained
nodes.statement: If the complete R166 witness, R167 token-lineage/operational architecture, and every R168 effect, coverage, regularity and triage premise hold on one common actual episode, the stochastic/continuous evidence refines W4-W5 for that declared relation. It does not replace physical realization, identify neural completeness, derive C1, validate B_min, or create a basal-experience gate.
nodes.domain: One common actual P/I/K/D/rho episode and one fixed stochastic effect/coverage certificate satisfying all premises simultaneously.
nodes.scope: One common actual P/I/K/D/rho episode and one fixed stochastic effect/coverage certificate satisfying all premises simultaneously.
nodes.source_lineage: Conditional refinement of R166-R167 application boundary; no reverse inference to experience existence or familiar mineness.
nodes.proof: Bind the stochastic laws, physical routes, context geometry and all validity clauses to the same episode; use R168 triage only inside R167 W4-W5 and retain W1-W3/W6 unchanged.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Any unsupported metric, L, lift, sensitivity, route, identity or upper/lower bound blocks the refinement; abstract kernels do not install themselves.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: one actual declared operational relation with stochastic consumer evidence
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: every all-of premise holds on the same application; no universal necessity or familiar-mineness conclusion
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same P/I lineage and indexed subinterval; actual routes, laws, samples, partial views, Phi/h and reports remain typed separately
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Extend operational installation evidence without weakening physical or semantic boundaries

rules.statement: The sharp effect envelope, explicit hidden-fiber obstruction and a valid lift contract jointly yield the delta+C h_X hidden-context coverage penalty and effect bound.
rules.proof_sketch: The lift contract supplies actual-context fill radius by triangle inequality; the sharp envelope converts that radius and tested upper bounds into an amplitude bound, while the obstruction prevents omitting delta.

same bounded L-Lipschitz effect and tested upper bounds
formal_contract_R168.quantification: Every hidden context is covered only through all simultaneous premises.

rules.statement: R167 validity discipline plus the typed stochastic effect, sharp actual/partial coverage envelope, random mass bound and amplitude/mass separation jointly require the five-way R168 status logic.
rules.proof_sketch: Positive lower evidence supports local use; universal envelope upper evidence supports bounded amplitude refutation; random no-hit evidence alone supports only a mass bound; invalid or incomplete premises block promotion.

fixed mu and sensitivity for mass statements
formal_contract_R168.quantification: Every validity clause precedes status; each conclusion keeps its local, universal-envelope or measure quantifier.
